entries.name: Employee relations investigations
entries.definition: Investigating workplace complaints and suspected misconduct, such as harassment or policy breaches, to establish the facts and recommend action.

entries.name: Employer branding
entries.definition: Shaping and promoting how an organisation is seen as a place to work, in order to attract and keep employees.

entries.name: Employment compliance
entries.definition: Making sure an organisation follows employment laws and regulations, such as those on pay, working hours and discrimination.

entries.name: EMS dispatch
entries.definition: Taking emergency calls and sending and coordinating ambulances and other emergency medical services.

entries.name: Encounter data management
entries.definition: Collecting, checking and submitting the records of healthcare visits and services, such as the encounter data that health plans report to government programs.

entries.name: Endevor
entries.definition: Software configuration management tool, from CA and now Broadcom, for controlling changes to source code and other components on mainframe systems.

entries.name: Endocannabinoid system
entries.definition: The network of cannabinoid receptors and naturally made cannabinoid-like molecules in the body that helps regulate functions such as mood, appetite, pain and sleep.

entries.name: Endocrine disorders
entries.definition: Medical knowledge of conditions caused by hormone-producing glands working abnormally, such as diabetes and thyroid disease.

entries.name: Endodontics
entries.definition: The dental specialty concerned with diseases of the tooth pulp and the tissues around the tooth root, including root canal treatment.

entries.name: Endotracheal suctioning
entries.definition: Clearing secretions from the airway of a patient with an endotracheal tube by passing a suction catheter through the tube.

entries.name: Endovascular aneurysm repair
entries.definition: A minimally invasive procedure that repairs an aortic aneurysm by placing a stent graft inside the vessel through small incisions in the groin.

entries.name: Endpoint detection and response
entries.definition: Security software that continuously monitors computers and other endpoints for suspicious activity and helps investigate and respond to threats.

entries.name: Endpoint engineering
entries.definition: Designing, deploying and maintaining the configuration, software and security controls of an organisation's end-user devices such as laptops and phones.

entries.name: Endpoint management
entries.definition: Configuring, patching, monitoring and securing the end-user devices of an organisation from a central point.

entries.name: Endpoint security
entries.definition: Protecting end-user devices such as laptops, servers and phones from malware, intrusion and data loss.

entries.name: Enema administration
entries.definition: Giving a patient fluid through the rectum to empty the bowel or to deliver medicine.

entries.name: Energy control procedures
entries.definition: Written steps for shutting down, isolating and locking out the hazardous energy sources of a machine before anyone services it.

entries.name: Energy system transition
entries.definition: The shift of energy production and use from fossil fuels to low-carbon and renewable sources.

entries.name: Engineered materials arrestor system
entries.definition: A runway-end safety system of crushable concrete blocks that slows and stops an aircraft that overruns the runway.

entries.name: Engineering drawing
entries.definition: Preparing or reading technical drawings that follow standard conventions to show the shape, dimensions and tolerances of parts and assemblies.

entries.name: Engineering economics
entries.definition: The application of economic analysis, such as cost-benefit comparison, present worth and break-even analysis, to engineering decisions.

entries.name: Engineering education
entries.definition: The teaching of engineering and the study of how engineering is best learned.

entries.name: Engineering mathematics
entries.definition: The mathematics, such as calculus, linear algebra and differential equations, used to model and solve engineering problems.

entries.name: Engineering statics
entries.definition: The branch of mechanics that analyses the forces on structures and bodies that are at rest.

entries.name: Engineering statistics
entries.definition: The use of statistical methods, such as design of experiments, reliability analysis and quality control, to solve engineering problems.

entries.name: Enhanced Data rates for GSM Evolution
entries.definition: A mobile data technology that raises data rates on GSM networks, often called 2.75G.

entries.name: Enhanced prudential standards
entries.definition: US Federal Reserve rules, required by the Dodd-Frank Act, that set stricter capital, liquidity and risk-management requirements for large bank holding companies.

entries.name: eNodeB
entries.definition: The base station in a 4G LTE radio network that connects mobile devices to the core network.

entries.name: Enscape
entries.definition: Real-time rendering and virtual-reality software that works inside architectural design programs such as Revit and SketchUp.

entries.name: Ensemble conducting
entries.definition: Directing a group of musicians, such as an orchestra, band or choir, in rehearsal and performance by setting tempo, giving cues and shaping the interpretation.

entries.name: Ensemble methods
entries.definition: Machine learning techniques that combine the predictions of several models, as in bagging, boosting and stacking, to get a more accurate result.

entries.name: Enterprise integration
entries.definition: Connecting an organisation's separate applications and data sources so that they exchange data and work together.

entries.name: Enterprise network security
entries.definition: Protecting an organisation's networks and the systems on them from attack, misuse and unauthorised access.

entries.name: Enterprise performance management
entries.definition: The processes and software an organisation uses to plan, budget, forecast and report on its financial and operating performance.

entries.name: EnterpriseDB
entries.definition: A commercial database product, built on PostgreSQL with added enterprise features and Oracle compatibility, from the company EnterpriseDB (EDB).

entries.name: Entrepreneurial Operating System
entries.definition: A business management system from Gino Wickman, set out in the book Traction, that organises a company around vision, people, data, issues, process and traction.

entries.name: Environmental anthropology
entries.definition: The study of the relationships between human societies and their natural environments.

entries.name: Environmental finance
entries.definition: The area of finance concerned with environmental issues, such as carbon markets, green bonds and funding for conservation and clean energy.

entries.name: Environmental impact statement preparation
entries.definition: Researching and writing the report, such as one required under the US National Environmental Policy Act, that assesses the significant environmental effects of a proposed project.

entries.name: Environmental journalism
entries.definition: Reporting and writing news about the environment, climate and natural resources.
